title: What is known about 1RB0RA_1RC0RD_1RD0LC_1LE1RA_---1LF_1RB0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_1RC0RD_1RD0LC_1LE1RA_---1LF_1RB0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a few long runs of the word 110 separated by short groups of 0s. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells) finds no halt in the first 1012 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,953 cells have been visited and 2,625 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.329). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.331).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells) runs 1012 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Runs of 110 cut by a marker
claims.text: At the moments the head reaches a new cell between steps 9.81·107 and 108, the tape is mostly two long runs of 110; at the right-end moments a marker cuts the first run into 214 + 100, 173 + 142, 158 + 158 copies.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state E was entered 12,465,925 times, always reading a 1 (E0 halts).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is a few long runs of 110 separated by short groups of 0s; a marker cuts the first run at a point that moves from round to round, and a solid tail on the right grows two cells at a time.

facts.text: No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells).
The tape is mostly long runs of 110, cut by a moving marker.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 3,953 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With b for 110, around step 9.8·107:

The bulk of the tape is two long runs of 110 (317 and 280 copies, then 318 and 281). At the left-end moments the first run is whole; at the right-end moments a marker 1 0^2 1 0 cuts it into two pieces whose lengths add up to about the same total (214 + 100, 173 + 142, 158 + 158), and the cut point moves from one round to the next. Each round adds about one copy to each long run, and the solid stretch at the right end grows (1^9, 1^13, 1^17 at the moments above). After 108 steps 1,835 cells have been visited.
What the marker computes has not been worked out.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is E reading a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 0 (1LE), so a halt needs 0 D>0: D on a 0 with another 0 just to its left. In the first 108 steps E was entered 12,465,925 times, every time on a 1, and 12,464,368 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.
The tape does hold groups of several 0s (0^3, 0^5, 0^6), so the constraint is not just that 0s are isolated: D has to arrive there in the wrong phase. Whether it ever does is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.329). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.331).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,953 cells (1,088 left of the start, 2,124 right), with a density of 1s of 0.664.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: a sea of 110 blocks cut by a moving marker
summary: Its tape is a few long runs of 110 separated by short groups of 0s; a marker cuts the first run at a point that moves from round to round, and a solid tail on the right grows two cells at a time.
